title: Real-time self-supervised denoising for high-speed fluorescence neural imaging
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Denoise the original neural fluorescence recordings while preserving fast voltage/calcium dynamics and source real-time constraints. The real voltage fidelity endpoint compares denoised pixel fluorescence traces with simultaneous electrophysiology, not with a fabricated clean fluorescence image.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Denoise the original neural fluorescence recordings while preserving fast voltage/calcium dynamics and source real-time constraints. The real voltage fidelity endpoint compares denoised pixel fluorescence traces with simultaneous electrophysiology, not with a fabricated clean fluorescence image.

Source-paper comparison for Original Figure 3f denoised-fluorescence/electrophysiology Pearson correlation, with source fidelity and speed constraints; exact aggregate unresolved: Figure 3f uses Pearson correlation r=sum((x-xbar)(y-ybar))/sqrt(sum((x-xbar)^2)sum((y-ybar)^2)) between single-pixel ΔF/F and synchronized electrophysiology. Figure 3b analogously compares simulated traces with clean truth; image PSNR/SSIM and throughput are distinct outcomes.
success_criteria: Recover the exact real-recording author baseline, original pixel/ROI roster, preprocessing, correlation aggregation and permitted same-stack training protocol.
Compare candidate and FAST on identical original recordings and label access, with predeclared meaningful temporal-fidelity gain and valid uncertainty.
Preserve original real calcium and voltage scope; synthetic controls or a favorable selected pixel/recording cannot replace it.
Retain spike fidelity, matched temporal context and hardware-bound end-to-end resource measurements; faster inference or smoother traces alone are insufficient.
Treat the existing group-disjoint evaluator as an extension unless exact source equivalence is independently established; changed splits never count as original-task victory.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
